focus: Complete the CLI session-continuity audit across supported and unsupported runtime packages; separate single-session resume, explicit-id resume, fork, and detached parallel work.
keyQuestions: Which remaining packages outside deep-loop contain genuinely answer-dependent or user-visible restart/compaction scenarios?
Which runtime-specific scenarios need to split because the runner lacks a matching adapter or action?
Which conversion, update and coverage candidates provide the highest operator or release risk reduction for their authoring and execution cost?
answeredQuestions: Which existing CLI continuity cases need more than one exchange and qualify at Q2?
Which of those can the shared runner execute and which command-level details remain outside its exact surface?
Which apparent multi-session scenarios are not conversational and stay Q4?

label: Codex CX-017, Claude Code CC-015/CC-016, OpenCode CO-018/CO-019, and Devin resume-continue all meet Q2: each needs a follow-up exchange that uses prior session state or an explicitly captured session id. Add shared-runner conversation companions for supported interactive-session continuity, but keep each existing headless CLI flag/ID check as primary evidence because runner restart resumes its own session and does not invoke every exact `-p`, `exec resume`, `--continue`, or `-s` command.

Cursor CU-015/CU-016 and Hermes HERMES-011 are also Q2 because Turn 2 must recover a prior session, but keep them manual. Cursor and Hermes are not among the validator's accepted conversation runtimes, so a JSON block cannot currently be run without an out-of-scope adapter addition. Track these as adapter-dependent candidates rather than rewriting their exact CLI checks.

Keep OpenCode CO-020 fork-and-share manual. The second dispatch must branch from a parent into a distinct session, making it Q2, but the JSON schema exposes only restart and compact actions and its runner adapter resumes the same session. Until fork is a supported conversation action, a JSON rewrite would not test the new session-id invariant.

Keep OpenCode CO-026 parallel-detached-session and CO-027 worker-farm-loop as single-prompt command scenarios. They launch independent sessions and verify IDs/files with shell output, but do not depend on a later user answer or continuation of one session; several workers are not a multi-turn conversation. Their OpenCode-version constraints and `< /dev/null` regression are better served by the present command harness.

Rank CO-019, CC-016 and CX-017 highest among CLI continuity updates because explicit session-id resume prevents confusion between the latest session and the intended one; add CC-015, CO-018 and Devin as same-session companions. Value is high, authoring cost is low-to-medium, and execution cost is medium per supported runtime. Defer Cursor/Hermes and OpenCode fork until adapters/actions exist; retain detached worker tests at Q4.
